newsitem.title: ALBANIA: Albania president to attend anti-violence rally.
newsitem.headline: Albania president to attend anti-violence rally.

text.p: Albanian President Sali Berisha, in his first public appearance on the streets of Tirana since unrest gripped the Balkan country, was due to address a rally on Tuesday to denounce the spread of violence.

Berisha, who was granted special powers on Sunday to use the military to restore order, was scheduled to head a gathering at the town hall on central Skanderbeg Square, where protesters battled with riot police two days ago.
In an apparent bid to avoid any escalation of violence, his ruling Democratic Party dropped original plans to stage the protest outside the headquarters of the opposition Socialists.
An Democratic Party official said a news conference at noon (1100 GMT) by Interior Minister Halit Shamata had been cancelled as Berisha would attend the rally.

The Democrats, who won a landslide victory in controversial elections last May, are seeking to regain control after two weeks of disturbances sparked by growing anger over the collapse of pyramid investment schemes into which thousands sank their savings.

The Democrats have angrily accused the rival Socialists, former communists, of inciting trouble, especially in southern towns where demonstrators set fire to scores of public buildings at the weekend.

In an apparent attempt to calm the atmosphere, Tuesday's rally was switched from outside the Socialist Party office to the other side of Skanderbeg Square, where party supporters were expected to repair damage caused during Sunday's clashes.
"The Democratic party has decided to change the rally... into a constructive rally against violence and destruction," Albanian state television said.
Central Tirana appeared calm on Tuesday but armed soldiers remained on guard outside ministries and the central bank.
"The "red gangs' are responsible for all this trouble," one elderly man said in a street adjacent to Skanderbeg Square.
But another man, aged 28, said he did not believe what he had heard on television.
"Berisha said after the elections (last May) that communism was dead. So it can't be the communists who are stirring the trouble but the Democrats themselves," he said.
Albania's main opposition parties have accused the Democrats of using pyramid scheme money to fund their campaigns for national and local elections last year.
The Democrats have sought to switch the public's attention away from the collapsing investment schemes by invoking what Albanian television called "the red terror".
On the eve of the government rally, a senior Socialist party figure and former deputy, Ndre Legisi, suffered a fractured skull after he was attacked by three or four men in central Tirana.
Doctors said Legisi was in a critical condition. The motives for the attack were not immediately clear.
Economists estimate that almost all Albanians are directly, or indirectly affected by the collapse of the pyramid schemes, with many people facing financial ruin.
